transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-05-14
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Ava Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Morales (Redwood CSM), Priya Patel (Redwood SE), Michael Hart (CloverCity CTO), Sonia Gupta (Head of Data), Elliot Rivera (DevOps)

Summary: quick onboarding kickoff to align on architecture, security requirements, timeline for pilot, and next steps. Discussed Hosted vs Dedicated, VPC options, SOC2/KMS, and scheduling a deep technical run.

Topics: onboarding plan, architecture, security/compliance, benchmarking, pilot scope, timelines

Transcript:
[00:00] Ava Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh i'm ava from redwood, i'll kick us off. can folks just say hi and roles real quick?
[00:06] Michael Hart: michael here, cto at clover city, we're looking to integrate llm features into patient triage, so happy to be here.
[00:12] Sonia Gupta: sonia, head of data, i'll own the data flows and privacy bits.
[00:16] Elliot Rivera: elliot, devops, i'll help with infra and networking.
[00:19] Diego Morales: diego from redwood cs — i'll be your csm for the onboarding.
[00:23] Priya Patel: priya, solutions eng, i'll run the tech deep dives and benchmarks.
[00:27] Ava Chen: great, thanks. quick agenda — we want to confirm goals for the pilot, security needs, what type of deployment you want (hosted vs dedicated vs private), timelines, and then next steps.

[02:01] Michael Hart: our main success criteria are latency under 200ms p95 for short prompts, cost at or below our current gpt-3.5 spend per query, and data never stored outside US. timeline: pilot in next 2 weeks ideally.

[03:18] Sonia Gupta: also SOC2 is required, and we need audit logs and KMS integration. we do SSO with okta so SAML is a must.

[04:05] Priya Patel: absolutely; redwood supports sso/saml and we have integrations with customer-managed kms/hsm for private installs and dedicated supports vpc peering. our default hosted API is in multi-region but we can restrict to us-only regions for data residency.

[05:30] Elliot Rivera: how does dedicated differ from hosted for us? we care about predictable throughput more than absolute lowest price.

[05:35] Ava Chen: good question — dedicated gives you reserved gpu pools, deterministic throughput and isolation; hosted is multi-tenant and is easiest to start with. for latency/p95 and consistent performance, dedicated is recommended. but, it requires commit/contract and takes a few days to provision.

[07:00] Michael Hart: provisioning time — how long?

[07:04] Priya Patel: typically 48-72 hours once we have network details and routing; if you need VPC peering or on-prem packages that can add steps. for a quick pilot we can spin a small dedicated pool in a us region.

[08:20] Sonia Gupta: are request logs retained? we need audit log retention for 1 year and ability to export.

[08:30] Diego Morales: yes, we have configurable retention and can provide exported logs; enterprise tiers include longer retention windows and access to SIEM integrations. i'll include the specifics in the security pack.

[09:12] Elliot Rivera: about kms — do you support customer-managed keys?

[09:18] Priya Patel: yes, we support kms/hsm integrations for our private and dedicated offerings; hosted can also integrate with a bring-your-own-key model depending on contract. small note: there are some limitations on how keys are rotated for streaming workloads but we can document the flow.

[11:00] Michael Hart: okay on the technical reqs. next, benchmarks — we have sample payloads, mainly short prompts (50-150 tokens) with some longer summarization. can you run an initial benchmark and share p95 and token costs?

[11:32] Priya Patel: yes, please send the payloads; we'll run them against a few model variants and both hosted/dedicated configs. typical deliverable: latency table, token counts, cost per 1k tokens, and config recommendations.

[13:00] Sonia Gupta: data residency — we need confirmation that, during pilot, no data leaves the us. is that possible on hosted?

[13:15] Ava Chen: yes, we can pin the region to US-only for hosted, but for full compliance we usually recommend dedicated or private. hosted regional pinning is good for initial tests.

[14:40] Michael Hart: any concerns about hallucination/regression over time? we need a way to monitor quality.

[14:50] Priya Patel: redwood optimize offers quality monitoring tied to prompt sets and automatic regression alerts; we can tie that into your test harness and run periodic evals. we'll demo that in the deep dive.

[16:05] Elliot Rivera: network — we use strict egress rules. what does onboarding need from our side to set up peering?

[16:15] Priya Patel: we'll need CIDR blocks, a point-to-point IP, allowed ports, and SAML metadata for SSO. for peering there's a short checklist — i'll send that.

[17:40] Diego Morales: to recap the pilot proposal: 2-week dedicated trial in us-east, redwood will run benchmarks with customer payloads, we'll enable audit logs and KMS integration, and devops will have a dedicated contact to provision networking. does that align?

[18:02] Michael Hart: yes that sounds good. budget — what's the expected cost model for the trial?

[18:10] Ava Chen: trial pricing is typically a small reserved credit — we'll include detailed pricing by model in the doc. main levers: batching, quantization profile, and model choice will affect unit cost.

[19:50] Sonia Gupta: any compliance docs you can share now?

[19:55] Diego Morales: i'll upload SOC2, ISO summary, encryption whitepaper, and our runbook for dedicated/private. expect an email with links after this call.

[21:20] Michael Hart: what about SAML SSO for user access to the console and audit trail?

[21:30] Priya Patel: we support SAML and SCIM for user provisioning; role-based access control is configurable by team. we'll share the SSO setup guide.

[22:40] Elliot Rivera: is there an SDK best practice for lower latency? we're using node for backend endpoints.

[22:48] Priya Patel: yes — use streaming responses and persistent connections, enable KV cache for multi-turn chat to avoid re-sending context, and our SDK has connection pooling options. i'll send a node example.

[24:02] Michael Hart: any gotchas with HIPAA? we're not fully hipaa yet but evaluating.

[24:10] Diego Morales: we have HIPAA guidance; private deployments are the recommended path for PHI. we'll attach the compliance summary.

[25:40] Sonia Gupta: timeline again — you said 48-72 hours to provision dedicated after network info, pilot in 2 weeks — can you meet that?

[25:50] Priya Patel: yes assuming we get network/CIDR and SSO metadata and samples by Tuesday, we can provision by Thursday and kick off benchmarks Friday or Monday at latest.

[27:10] Michael Hart: ok we'll aim to send the artifacts tomorrow.

[28:30] Ava Chen: just to capture risks — provisioning delays if firewall rules need change, cost ramp if model choice isn't tuned, and any legal review that delays KMS or data residency sign-off.

[29:05] Elliot Rivera: sounds fair. on legal, who do we loop in from redwood?

[29:12] Diego Morales: i'll be the initial contact; contract/legal will be cc'd once we land on pilot terms.

[30:40] Sonia Gupta: do you have reference customers in healthcare? we want to see similar use cases.

[30:48] Ava Chen: yes, we'll share a short list and anonymized benchmarks — i'll include links in the follow-up.

[32:00] Priya Patel: next steps for the technical team: send sample payloads, traffic patterns, and SSO metadata. we'll schedule a separate deep dive for the benchmark run.

[33:15] Michael Hart: can you also send an architecture diagram for the dedicated setup and an onboarding checklist?

[33:22] Diego Morales: yes — onboarding checklist, network checklist, and security docs will go out in one package.

[34:30] Elliot Rivera: one more question — do you support private on-prem installs? we're exploring for later.

[34:37] Priya Patel: we do; private offers on-prem packaging and air-gapped options, but that's a longer lead and is scoped separately.

[35:55] Michael Hart: ok, final item — can we get a clear SLO for p95 latency on the trial? we need that for internal acceptance criteria.

[36:05] Priya Patel: we'll include a targeted p95 for the selected model and configuration; for short prompts we typically see 100-200ms p95 on dedicated, but we'll run the benchmark and publish the exact numbers.

[37:20] Diego Morales: i've noted the actions, and i'll follow up with calendar invites for the deep dive and a 30-minute onboarding runbook review.

[38:45] Ava Chen: great — any blockers from clover city?

[38:50] Michael Hart: none immediate — just need to get the artifacts together.

[40:05] Sonia Gupta: timeline for docs?

[40:10] Diego Morales: i'll send the security pack and onboarding docs by EOD tomorrow.

[41:30] Ava Chen: cool. let's recap real quick: 1) clover city to send samples + network + sso; 2) redwood to provision 2-week dedicated trial in us-east and run benchmarks; 3) redwood to send SOC2/security docs and onboarding checklist; 4) schedule technical deep dive with priya and elliot next week.

[42:10] Michael Hart: yep that's good. thanks everyone.

[42:18] Priya Patel: thanks, will follow up with meeting invite for deep dive.

[42:21] Diego Morales: thanks all.

[42:25] Meeting end
